title: Byte sizes with iota
hints: `iota` is 0 on the first line of the block. You want `KB` on the line where `iota == 1`, so put `_ = iota` first.
Write the expression once: `KB = 1 << (10 * iota)`, then `MB`, `GB`, `TB` on their own lines repeat it with iota = 2, 3, 4.
In `HumanSize`, let `f := float64(n)` and test `n >= TB`, then `GB`, `MB`, `KB`, returning `fmt.Sprintf("%.1f TB", f/TB)` etc. The fallback is `fmt.Sprintf("%d B", n)`. Don't forget `import "fmt"`.
